prompt: A work colleague has asked you to swap shifts for the third week in a row. You are tired, you need the day off you planned, and you feel guilty saying no. What response keeps both kindness and a healthy boundary?

options.text: Warmly decline this time, explain you need the day off, and offer to help them find other cover or swap on a future date if you can
Say yes again and push through, then feel resentful towards them all week
Say no coldly and complain to other colleagues about how often they ask
Ignore the message and hope they find someone else

explanation: A clear, warm no protects your rest without punishing your colleague. Saying yes while resentful, going cold, or going silent all damage the working relationship more than an honest boundary does.
